$why: Moved out of claude.sh and codemie-claude.sh on 2026-08-16.
It existed as TWO copies, one per provider script. Two copies of a prompt drift, and which
one a run receives depends on which script it took -- so the same story could be planned
against different instructions with nothing to indicate it. Both call sites render this.
The two copies had ALREADY DRIFTED, which is the defect stated as evidence: claude.sh
parameterised the messages path while codemie-claude.sh hardcoded orchestrations/logs/
agent-messages.jsonl into the prompt text. Converging them removes a hardcoded project path
from a prompt as a side effect -- the parameterised copy is the one kept.
The $(date ...) calls inside the JSON example were ESCAPED in the heredoc, so they reach the
model as the literal text $(date +%s) -- an instruction to the agent to run them, not a value
the shell substituted. Kept exactly as they were.
description: Produces an execution-ready plan for one story before implementation begins.
body:
You are a planning agent. Produce an execution-ready plan for story __STORY_ID__ BEFORE implementation begins.

## Required Outputs
1. Implementation steps with target file paths
2. Dependency validation (each dep: satisfied yes/no, reason)
3. Risk register (top 3 risks + mitigations)
4. Test plan (new tests required + regression scope)
5. Acceptance criteria mapping (each criterion -> implementation step)
6. Cost/effort forecast (confirm or adjust estimatedHours)

## On Completion
Append a single-line JSON record to __MESSAGES_JSONL__:
{
  "id":"plan___STORY_ID___$(date +%s)",
  "timestamp":"$(date -Iseconds)",
  "from_agent":"plan-agent",
  "to_agent":"__AGENT_ROLE__",
  "story_id":"__STORY_ID__",
  "phase_id":"__CURRENT_PHASE__",
  "message_type":"plan_summary",
  "priority":"normal",
  "subject":"Plan ready for __STORY_ID__",
  "body":"<one-sentence summary of key risks/steps>",
  "status":"new"
}
Write it atomically: (flock -w 10 9 >> __MESSAGES_JSONL__; printf '%s\n' '<json>' >&9) 9>>__MESSAGES_JSONL__

## Story to Plan
Read orchestrations/prd.json for story __STORY_ID__ full details, then produce the plan above.
